key_insight: Pre-AF 13 is an interpretable 13-feature model that predicts medium-term atrial fibrillation risk from routine discharge reports in cardiovascular patients.
clinical_relevance: It could help hospitals flag higher-risk patients earlier using existing EHR data, potentially improving AF surveillance beyond standard clinical risk scores.
method: Retrospective single-center EHR study of 17,562 cardiovascular patients without prior AF.
NLP pipeline converted discharge notes into 73 structured variables, then LightAutoML built full, simplified, and linear risk models.
Model performance was assessed with ROC AUC and compared against CHARGE-AF, C2HEST, MHS, and HAVOC; SHAP was used for interpretation.
evidence_signal: Among 80,576 records, 1,438 patients (8.19%) developed AF; the best models achieved ROC AUC 0.735 for 24-month prediction and 0.696 across full follow-up, outperforming the comparator clinical scores.
watch_item: The study is single-center and retrospective, so external validation and prospective testing are needed before real-world use.
paper_title: Pre-AF 13: An Interpretable Atrial Fibrillation Risk Score Mined from Discharge Reports
